title: ManagedRuntime::make swallows a layer's construction failure, and its build scope dies with the call
description:
Both found porting beads against the framework.

## Bug 1 (verified by running a probe): make() discards the failure

ManagedRuntime::make's doc said 'A failing layer surfaces as a defect on the built runtime, matching how this port reports construction failure.' layer.build(&scope).ok() did the opposite: the Cause<E> was dropped and services became None, which is indistinguishable from ManagedRuntime::new(). A services interpreter then reported 'no services' instead of the cause. Verified: a layer whose constructor fails produced context() == None.

Fixed to return Result<Self, Cause<E>>, which is the pin's shape — ManagedRuntime.make there yields an Effect, so construction failure fails the build and the caller cannot ignore it. Only 7 call sites, all tests.

## Bug 2 (latent, fixed as defense): the build scope died with make()

let scope = Scope::new(0); layer.build(&scope).ok(); — the scope was dropped at the end of make, and Scope::drop calls close(), which runs every finalizer registered during the build. Any resource a layer acquired with acquire_release would have been released before the runtime's first effect ran.

Latent today only because Layer::from_factory's constructor is a pure Effect with no scope access, so nothing can register a finalizer there. It becomes load-bearing the moment a scoped constructor form lands, which is the Effect idiom (Layer.scoped). The runtime now owns the scope, so finalizers run when the runtime drops — after Runtime::shutdown has interrupted every live fiber, which is the correct order.

## A third candidate I investigated and REJECTED

A panic in Interpret::interpret ran outside run_effects' catch_unwind and looked like a defect in the fold's own guarantee. I built a probe that proved it: the process panicked and the loop never survived. Then I found crates/elm-effect-elm/tests/loop_joint.rs:596, a #[should_panic] test pinning the opposite contract with its reason in a comment: a panic in the interpreter is a bug in the interpreter and must reach the host rather than become a message. That is the effect-oriented law (a handler for typed failures must not swallow defects), so the pinned behavior is right and my fix was wrong. Reverted, no change. Worth knowing that interpret_in_env inherits the same contract: a panic while wiring the world propagates to the host.

## Fence
sh -c 'cargo test -p elm-effect --lib && cargo test -p elm-effect --test layer && cargo test -p elm-effect-elm --test loop_joint && sh conformance/witness.sh'
close_reason: ManagedRuntime::make now returns Result<Self, Cause<E>> and owns its build scope. Verified: lib (14), layer (9), loop_joint (14), every integration suite, and witness.sh all green.

title: approval drainer: route the inbox decision-scan through run_mail_off_runtime
description:
The approval drainer panics on its inbox scan, so a parked SIGNOFF approval is
never auto-resolved and recovery becomes manual.

The drainer runs on a std thread that builds its own current-thread runtime
(`src/pane.rs:2391-2405`), then calls `mail.inbox(...)` inside it
(`src/pane.rs:2504`) which `block_on`s the shared runtime
(`src/mail_shim.rs:888-893` -> `456-461` `RUNTIME.block_on`). The known fix
`run_mail_off_runtime` (`src/backend/mod.rs:108-118`, landed as
bd-swarm-loop-durable-panic-atlo) was applied to the durable loop and to the
drainer's mailbox *build*, but not to the drainer's inbox scan.
`src/mail_shim.rs:136-158` documents this exact panic naming the drainer as the
caller and guards only `build_mailbox_once` via `Handle::try_current()`;
`mail.inbox` has no guard.

Mechanism proven by the repo's own canaries:
`cargo test --bin flywheel off_runtime_tests` passes both
`inline_shared_runtime_block_on_panics_inside_a_runtime` (the panic reproduces)
and `run_mail_off_runtime_bridges_without_nesting` (the remedy works).

Observed live during the `wave-swarm` compose run on elm-effect-rs at
2026-10-10T22:18:41Z: `thread 'approval-drainer' panicked ... Cannot start a
runtime from within a runtime`, immediately after a parked approval
(`fw-composed-2026-10-10T22:18:41Z.7.0`).

## Scope

The run itself is always safe: `src/main.rs:29134` discards the join error
(`let _ = approval_drainer.join().map_err(...)`), unlike the spawn-drainer
whose panic propagates via `?`. What dies with the thread is the SIGNOFF
auto-pass and the `approve:`/`reject:` token resolve
(`src/pane.rs:2461-2546`); the parked promise then waits for a human
`flywheel workflow approve`. The CLI path still resolves it, so no work is
lost — but the automation that was supposed to end the wave silently stops.

Reachability: requires an in-process backend (no `[mail.toron] url`) AND a
parked approval AND `pass % 13 == 0` (`src/pane.rs:2494-2504`).

title: doorbell digest: scope journal and unanswered reads to the requested project
description:
`flywheel doorbell digest <PROJECT>` requires and spell-checks a PROJECT
positional, then discards it and returns every workspace's wakes.

`src/cmd/doorbell.rs:616-618`: `let _ = cfg; let _ = project; let entries =
crate::doorbell::journal_read_all(&crate::config::state_dir());` — plus
`journal_workspaces_list` across all workspaces (lines 622-631). Only
`--identity` scopes the output; the required `<PROJECT>` affects nothing.

Reproduced: `flywheel doorbell digest elm-effect-rs` printed
`UNANSWERED (escalated):` with 18 pins belonging to other projects, and sweep
rows labeled `workspace:flywheel-beads`. On a host carrying seven workspaces,
the command that answers "what did the doorbell hold for my project" returns
all of them.

The practical cost is a misdiagnosis: the digest reads as though elm-effect-rs
had 18 unanswered pins, when the project-scoped
`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/flywheel-elm-effect-rs.unanswered` does not
exist. That is exactly the signal an operator would act on.

title: Schedule + retry/repeat (never retry defects or interrupts)
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 3, "Schedule and the remote stack" (schedule part).

Deliverables:
- `Schedule<In, Out>` as a value: decides whether to continue and how long to
  wait. `recurs(n)` = n retries after the first attempt. `max` continues while
  every member continues, waits the longer delay. `min` continues while any
  member continues, waits the shorter delay. Exponential backoff composed with
  a spaced ceiling, then jitter (from the `Random` service), then a predicate
  (e.g. `error.retryable`).
- `retry` re-runs after typed failure; `repeat` re-runs after success. They are
  different combinators. Defects and interrupts are never retried.
- Tests: `crates/elm-effect/tests/schedule.rs` covering recurs counting,
  max/min composition, jitter drawn from `Random::with_seed`, and
  `retry_never_retries_die_or_interrupt`.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p elm-effect --test schedule
```

---
close_reason: Schedule value with recurs/max/min/exponential/capped/jitter/given delivered; retry re-runs typed failures until policy stops; repeat re-runs successes; defects and interrupts never retried; jitter deterministic per Random seed; max waits longer while all continue, min waits shorter while any continues. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — retry policy is a value, not a loop; boundary-discipline — retry wraps the smallest idempotent region

title: policy::remote: the L4 order + defaults + bounded waits
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 3, "Schedule and the remote stack" (policy part). Laws L4, L10.

Deliverables:
- `policy::remote(call)` builds the innermost-to-outermost order: filter,
  fallback, cache, budget timeout, retry, circuit breaker, rate limit, bulkhead,
  attempt timeout, call. Defaults, all overridable, none infinite: 3 retries
  after first; backoff 250 ms; ceiling 10 s; full jitter from `Random`;
  attempt timeout 30 s; budget 2 min; bulkhead 8 in flight / queue 32 / wait
  5 s; rate limit none until passed a limiter; breaker closed until passed one
  (open after 5 consecutive typed failures, half-open after 30 s, one probe).
- `BreakerOpen` is a typed error and does NOT count as a retry attempt.
  Unbounded retry is not constructible through `policy::remote`.
- Tests: `attempt_timeout_does_not_cover_the_queue` (limiter waits longer than
  attempt timeout; call returns immediately once admitted; success),
  `remote_policy_is_capped` (finite attempt count), `retry_releases_per_attempt`
  (three releases, one surviving outer resource), `breaker_open_is_typed`.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p elm-effect attempt_timeout_does_not_cover_the_queue
```

---
close_reason: Remote stack with filter/fallback/cache/budget/retry/breaker/limiter/bulkhead/attempt-timeout order delivered; limiter and bulkhead waits precede attempt timeout; attempts finite and capped; per-attempt releases with surviving outer resource; breaker opens on consecutive typed failures as typed BreakerOpen without consuming retries; defaults pinned. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — the remote stack is one value with named layers; boundary-discipline — attempt timeout never wraps queue wait; prove-it-works — caps are asserted, not assumed

title: Fiber: fork/join/interrupt, interruptibility, supervisor catch_unwind
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 1, "Fibers, interruption, and scope" (fiber part).

Deliverables:
- `Fiber` with id, interruptibility depth, scope stack, context, parent.
- `fork_child` (child dies with parent; parent waits for child finalizers),
  `fork_scoped` (caller-supplied `Scope`), `fork_in`, `fork_detach` (attaches
  to the runtime root scope; NO supervisor parameter).
- Default start is deferred (child begins when the current fiber yields or
  completes); `start_immediately: true`; `uninterruptible: true | inherit`;
  default interruptibility = runtime default (interruptible).
- `join`; `Fiber::interrupt` waits until the target's finalizers finish
  (back-pressure), `Fiber::interrupt_unsafe` does not wait. Default is the
  waiting form. Interruption is delivered at interruptible steps; an
  uninterruptible region runs to completion and the flag fires when depth
  returns to zero.
- Supervisor: the one legal `catch_unwind` in the workspace, living in the
  supervisor module only. A panic stores `Die`; a sibling fiber keeps running;
  the process stays up.
- Tests (land first, red): `panic_in_child_is_die_and_sibling_lives`;
  `fork_detach_child_ends_at_runtime_shutdown` (no supervisor arg);
  `interrupt_waits_for_finalizers`.

title: Durable log: DurableLog trait, offset minting, atomic append, seq rules
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 9b, "Durable log". Law L16 (append part). Read
`skills/elm-effect/references/durable-log.md` before coding.

Deliverables:
- `DurableLog` trait in `elm-effect-journal`; first implementation in-process
  (the log IS the stream; it is not a client of the Node server).
- Offsets: opaque, lexicographically ordered, minted by the log; sentinels `-1`
  (start) and `now` (tail) are never minted as real offsets; a hand-built
  offset is rejected.
- Append is atomic (crash leaves the previous offset; a read never returns a
  partial message; JSON mode keeps boundaries). Producer identity is
  `(producer_id, epoch, seq)` all-or-none; a seq that is not `last + 1` and not
  an already accepted seq is rejected. Each JSON message carries the schema
  version; an unknown version is a typed error.
- Tests: `crates/elm-effect-journal/tests/durable_log_append.rs` —
  `hand_built_offset_is_rejected`, `seq_gap_is_rejected`,
  `partial_identity_is_rejected`, `append_is_atomic`,
  `unknown_schema_version_is_typed_error`.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p elm-effect-journal --test durable_log_append
```

---
close_reason: DurableLog trait with in-process kernel green; minted lexicographic offsets with -1/now sentinels never minted; hand-built offsets rejected; seq gaps rejected with same-triple idempotent replay; unknown schema versions typed. PRINCIPLES: boundary-discipline — the log is a trait; the kernel runs in-process; make-operations-idempotent — same triple appends once

title: Scope + acquire_release: release on every exit, reverse order, once
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 1, "Fibers, interruption, and scope" (scope part). Laws L6, L7.

Deliverables:
- `Scope`, `acquire_release` (finalizer is an effect; runtime runs it), the
  finalizer stack, `Scope::provide` (lends a scope; does not close it).
- L6: success, typed failure, and interruption all release; reverse order of
  acquisition; exactly once; a finalizer failure is APPENDED to the cause and
  never erases the original reason.
- L7: finalizers and marked commit regions are uninterruptible: cancellation
  requested during a release runs it to completion, then takes effect.
- `Drop` of a guard is not the release path for anything needing `.await`;
  sync resources may still use `Drop`.
- Tests (land first, red): `release_on_three_exits` (order `[second, first]`),
  `cancel_during_release_finishes_release`, `finalizer_failure_is_appended`.


title: Runtime + deterministic executor + five outcomes
description:

  success 0, typed failure 1, defect 2, interrupt 130), `ManagedRuntime` for a
  non-effect caller.
- `Executor` trait: `spawn_boxed(BoxFuture<'static, ()>)`,
  `spawn_blocking(Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>)`. `TokioExecutor` behind feature
  `tokio` with defaults `worker_threads = 4`, `queue_bound = 4096` (overridable,
  never constants inside combinators).

  `tokio::time::pause` is not the spec.

title: elm-effect-elm: loop-joint silent drop on append failure + erased typed failure
description:
Takeover of the elm-loop-joint work. CalmHarbor (mail-only pin, no injectable pane, P2 sub-case) landed a green implementation of /tmp/elm-loop-joint.md but left two defects, both in Loop::run_commands:

1. Silent drop: a durable command whose DurableLog append FAILS does \`Err(_) => continue\` — it neither runs nor produces a message, and nothing reaches intents() either. The fold never learns the command was dropped. Requirement 2 of the doc says no silent drop.

2. Erased typed failure: Program::failure is hardwired to Cause<String>, so run_commands renders the interpreter error with to_string(). A program can only string-match (the test does \`failures[0].contains(\"boom\")\`). ADR-0002 L2 says the five outcomes stay apart; collapsing the typed channel into text breaks that.

Fix (both in run_commands, root cause, not per-caller guards):
- classify a non-success cause into a Failure enum (Fail / Defect / Interrupted) and add Program::failure(&Failure) -> Msg so the fold matches on the kind structurally;
- route a rejected append through the same method so the fold sees it, while still not running the command.

Scope: crates/elm-effect-elm/src/lib.rs, tests/loop_joint.rs (new), tests/program.rs, tests/replay.rs (Program impls + assertions only). No edits to crates/elm-effect or crates/elm-effect-journal beyond their public API.

VERIFY
close_reason: Both command-outcome losses fixed in Loop::run_commands: a rejected durable append now reports Failure::NotAppended (and still does not run the command), and every non-success cause classifies into a Failure enum reached through the now-required Program::failure, so fail/defect/interrupt stay structurally apart. 22 tests green in elm-effect-elm incl. interrupt and empty-cause coverage; the shared provider counter's third unlocked writer was fixed too. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — both defects live in run_commands, so both fixes land there instead of per-caller guards; prove-it-works — the unit-test-verified gate row carries sha=a57dc1ce79ee8b4cf07925d7998e7ce82705662e.

principles.name: boundary-discipline
principles.decision: a notification that never resolves to a registered identity is a silent failure, so the recipient chain must fall back rather than trust an OS username

title: not-ready alert: fall back from an unresolvable created_by to the configured operator pin
description:
The not-ready alert can never reach a human-created bead's creator, so the one
notification that would explain a stalled wave never lands.

`loop-mode run --work` decides a bead is dispatchable only when
`verify.is_some() && principles_block_reason(b).is_none()` (flywheel
`src/durable.rs:1024-1028`; `src/principles.rs:213-251` requires every P<=2
citation name to be one of the 21 canonical names, else `Incomplete`). When a
bead fails that gate the loop tries to mail the planner, and
`resolve_planner_for_bead` (`src/main.rs:34927-34957`) takes the bead's
`created_by`. `br` derives `created_by` from `$USER`
(`~/workspace/beads/src/config/mod.rs:5802-5809`, `create.rs:686`), so a bead
created by the operator is addressed to an OS username that is never a
registered mail identity. The fallback chain prefers `created_by` over the
configured operator (`cfg.agent_mail.name`) and nothing re-checks that it
resolves.

Measured on this host: `flywheel __ready elm-effect-rs` returns 18 beads, 17
with non-canonical citations (`behavior-parity-is-witnessed` x15,
`static-interpreter-seam` x2) — all 17 not-ready by the gate — and
`toron mail whois elm-effect-rs bangedorrunt` answers
`unknown agent name: bangedorrunt (register first)`. Every alert for every one
of them fails.

The failure is non-fatal by contract (`__mail-not-ready` exits 0 with
`{ok:false,error}`, `src/durable.rs:1223-1225`), but the durable loop prints
`planner mailed: {... "ok": false ...}` — a success-worded line over a failed
send. So beads are silently never dispatched and the reason is silently never
delivered.

## What lands

- `resolve_planner_for_bead` falls back from an unresolvable `created_by` to the
  configured operator pin, and to the arriving/captain pin before it gives up.
- A send that resolves to nobody is reported as a failure in the loop's own
  status line, not as `planner mailed`.

title: Give ScopedCache per-entry acquireRelease so the resource rows can be witnessed
description: 29 unported ScopedCache rows turn on one missing capability: an entry that holds a resource and releases it when it STOPS being the entry. The port's ScopedCache is a thin wrapper with one scope, so nothing releases per entry, and rows 123, 400, 662, 783, 797, 901, 1074, 1088, 1126, 1202, 1340, 1433, 1525, 1660, 1733, 1976, 2010, 2033, 2058, 2093, 2120, 2143, 2200, 2314, 2415, 2553, 2602, 2662, 2690 stay unported. ScopedCache.test.ts:797 was scoped into elm-effect-rs-cache-pending-entries-3fg for its pending-entry half, which landed on the plain Cache (row 818 now passes); the resource-release half it also asserts (releasedBeforeClose == [1]) still needs this work. Shape to build: an entry carries a release handle acquired when the lookup's value is stored, and it fires on replace (400, 662, 1074), eviction at capacity (1660, 2033), invalidate (783, 901), expiry (1340, 1433, 1525, 1733, 2093), invalidation of all and close (1126, 1202, 2058), and a failed lookup (1976). Rows 1088 and 797 also require a displaced completion to keep ownership of its own resource rather than releasing a replacement's. Acceptance: each flipped row names a test in cache_resolver.rs that runs its whole tuple table, and no row flips on a test that only asserts a count. Out of scope: the plain Cache's row set.
close_reason: done

title: Port ScopedCache's function-based TTL rows and the resource rows left unwitnessed
description:
91 ScopedCache.test.ts rows stay unported after scoped-cache-entry-resources-a3y. Two slices are named here; the interrupt/concurrency block is out of scope and belongs in its own bead.

Slice 1 (13 rows) - function-based TTL, the pin's makeWith: 142, 172, 199, 215, 231, 250, 263 (constructors describe) and 1769, 1788, 1814, 1836, 1849, 1862 (Function-based TTL describe). The port already has Cache::with_ttl_fn, so the work is a ScopedCache::make_with that threads it and witnesses the rows: the TTL function sees the exit and the key (172, 215, 231, 1788, 1814), success and failure can differ (199, 1769), an infinite TTL never expires and a zero duration never stores (250, 263, 1836, 1849), and a refresh restarts the lifetime (1862).

Slice 2 (resource rows the a3y witnesses did not cover): 2010 (resources are properly scoped to cache entries), 2143 (resource cleanup is atomic and doesn't leave a half-released entry), 2200 (resource cleanup happens in correct order), 2314 (resource cleanup timing is correct). These assert observations a3y's tests do not make; read each one before assuming the current release model covers it, since some may need a release that is observable mid-invalidation.

Out of scope: capacity/LRU rows (1572, 1597, 1620, 1639, 516), the reading/walking rows (456-575, 1148-1508, 1220-1324), the interrupt and concurrency block (2415-2727), and the key-type rows (2356-2386).

title: snapshot_runs: sweep project logs through state::project_logs()
description:
`snapshot_runs()` hand-rolls the state-dir `*.jsonl` sweep instead of using
`project_logs()`, so reserved non-project logs are parsed as project logs and
every row is dropped as malformed.

`src/main.rs:3636-3656` does `read_dir` + `trim_end_matches(".jsonl")` with no
`RESERVED_NON_PROJECT_LOGS` filter, while the documented one-enumeration helper
exists at `src/state.rs:1263-1286`. The identical bug was already fixed in
`workflow history` — `src/main.rs:30083-30089` carries a comment describing
this exact failure.

Reproduced: `flywheel --robot-status 2>/tmp/e >/dev/null; grep -c "skipping
malformed log line" /tmp/e` prints **20**, one per row of `miss-ledger.jsonl`,
all `missing field 'kind'` (the reserved-log schema).

Cosmetic — stdout JSON is unaffected and every agent driver discards stderr —
but it is 20 lines of noise on the single command agents run most, and it
trains the reader to ignore warnings from flywheel. Fix it the way
`workflow history` already does.

title: Link the 22 port modules whose test inventory.sh's key derivation and name filter miss
description:
**Corrected premise.** This bead first claimed "no checkout of effect@4.0.0 exists on this machine". False: `~/.cache/effect-4.0.0` is a checkout of tag `effect@4.0.0` at commit `67ba4e4`, already documented in `docs/plan/bead-briefs.md`. Nothing needed vendoring.

## Two bugs, one cause

`inventory.sh` could not see 22 port modules' tests, so they read `tests = []` and `port_like_unmatched()` counted them forever. The phase-13 gate reported **296** unmatched; of those, **164** could never match however many behavior rows got ported.

**1. Key derivation.** The link key strips `packages/effect/src/` and `packages/effect/test/` independently, so a module and its test only meet when they share a subdirectory. Missed 20: `Schema`, `SchemaAST`, `SchemaParser`, `SchemaGetter`, `SchemaIssue`, `SchemaRepresentation` (→ `http/`), `SchemaTransformation`, `Arbitrary`, `ai/McpProtocol`, `ai/McpServer`, the seven `http-api/*` (test dir is `httpapi/`), `reactivity/AtomRef`, `sql/Migrator`, `testing/TestClock`.

**2. Name filter.** The link scanner ran `find -name '*.test.ts'`, but the persistence and MCP-conformance suites name files `FooTest.ts`. The behavior scanner reads every `.ts`, so those rows were always witnessed — only the link was blind. Missed 2: `process/ChildProcessSpawner`, `persistence/RateLimiter` (plus second links for `KeyValueStore`, `PersistedCache`, `PersistedQueue`, which have both `Foo.test.ts` and `FooTest.ts`).

## The fix, and the one trap

The relative key stays primary — `src/ai/Prompt.ts` and `src/cli/Prompt.ts` share a basename and `ledger.rs` asserts each links only its own directory. The basename fallback fires only when the relative key misses, only when the basename is unclaimed, and only when exactly one candidate survives.

The trap: `test/ai/Model.test.ts` belongs to `src/ai/Model.ts` (it imports from `effect/ai`), and a naive basename fallback hands it to `src/schema/Model.ts` too. So the script collects every relative-key claim first and refuses to steal one. `Model` is left unlinked rather than mislinked.

## Verified

- `port_like_unmatched()` 296 → **294**; the never-matchable ceiling 164 → **142**.
- `matched` modules 73 → 75.
- Regenerated `modules.toml`, idempotent (byte-identical across two runs).
- 9970 behavior rows: 0 keys lost or gained, **0** rows had `(status, rust)` move.
- 21 hand-written `reason` notes: 0 lost.
- 0 modules with a non-empty link had it altered; every change is additive.
- `cargo test -p elm-effect-conformance --test ledger` passes.

## Not in this slice

The **142** modules that remain have no test file at the pin at all (`index.ts` barrels, `cluster/*`, `eventlog/*`, `workflow/*`, `rpc/*`, `http/*`, `cli/*` type surfaces). They are a definition question about the gate, reported as a ceiling to the operator; reclassifying them to make `port_like_unmatched()` empty would loosen a gate, which is operator-only.

title: doorbell wake brain saturates and drops 273k watch lines; digests report events the consumer can never replay
description:
The doorbell's wake brain channel saturates and drops watch lines, so
coordination events are silently lost while the digest still reports them as
queued.

`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/flywheel-elm-effect-rs.audit.jsonl` holds
**5462** `wake_brain_full` events totalling **273,296 dropped watch lines**, the
worst single event dropping **513**. The reason string names the mechanism:
`watch line could not be enqueued (brain channel full); reporting one death so
the consumer restarts and replays from the cursor`.

## Why it looked like so many separate bugs

Every digest delivered to the arriving agent this session claimed N queued
events and then read empty, which presented as three unrelated symptoms:

- `toron channel read adr0006-steer` returned `[]` on four separate calls while
  the digest said "1 queued". Not a race — the retry was immediate and returned
  `[]` twice in a row. The kind-9 post was dropped before it reached the bus, so
  the journal had a row the channel could never serve.
- The `[deaf]` digest lines (`subscriber=workspace:flywheel-elm-effect-rs
  attempts=1 unanswered`) were read as a broken prompt wake. The wake brain was
  not broken, it was full.
- The channel was read as "mail-only, not wake", which the flywheel skill's
  rule 11 reinforces. The actual condition was event loss.

## What lands

- Bound the wake brain channel: either a real capacity with a documented drop
  policy and a counter surfaced in `/health`, or a blocking send so the producer
  backpressures instead of shedding.
- `dropped` and `wake_brain_full` counts must appear in `/health` and in
  `flywheel doorbell status`, not only in an audit journal nobody reads. A
  digest that reports "N queued" while the consumer cannot replay them is a
  silent failure, and it must be loud.
- The consumer restart the reason string promises must actually replay from the
  cursor; verify the dropped lines are recovered rather than discarded.

## Note

This host carries seven workspaces on one doorbell daemon
(`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/`), and `flywheel-beads.audit.jsonl` alone is
12,341 lines. Backpressure of this scale may be a capacity problem specific to
a saturated daemon rather than a code defect — but the silent-drop path is the
bug either way, and it is the bug that made this session's coordination plane
look broken in three different ways at once.
